contract_plain_english: Equation (1.8) presents a one-dimensional homogeneous conservation law: the time derivative of q plus the spatial derivative of its flux f(q) equals zero, with f identified as the flux function [printed p. 3, Section 1.1, (1.8) and following sentence]. The inherited unknown q is vector-valued, so one-dimensional concerns space rather than the number of conserved components [printed p. 1, paragraph following (1.1); printed p. 4, opening paragraph]. This passage specifies the equation's form rather than claiming that arbitrary functions satisfy it or asserting existence and uniqueness [printed p. 3, introduction to (1.8)]. The source separately qualifies derivation of this differential form from the integral conservation law by sufficient smoothness and acknowledges discontinuous solutions [printed p. 4, Section 1.1.2].
